Romanian leasing company, part of the BRD Groupe Societe Generale network, providing personalized financial and leasing solutions for vehicles and equipment in Romania. Its customers are businesses, entrepreneurs and professionals who finance cars, trucks and machinery, often arranged through dealerships and the bank's branches, and it earns interest and fees on leases. BRD, the parent bank, is listed on the Bucharest Stock Exchange and majority-owned by Societe Generale. Funding shown is 170 million in unspecified currency. B2B finance brand, with consumers meeting it via dealerships.

Enterprise file storage and collaboration company providing a cloud file services platform with a global file system for distributed organizations. Its software connects branch offices and remote sites to central cloud or on-premises object storage, replacing traditional file servers and backup, and is sold through partners such as IBM to enterprises, government and defence agencies. Co-founded by CEO Liran Eshel in 2008 in Israel, with research and development there, and based in New York, with about $180 million of funding. B2B IT brand.

Minneapolis-based cloud ERP and accounting software for small and mid-sized businesses, with customers across Asia-Pacific, the US and elsewhere. Products include Deskera Books, ERP, CRM, HRMS and manufacturing (MRP) modules, sold on subscription to firms that want one integrated system for invoicing, inventory, payroll and production. Founded in 2009 in Singapore by Shashank Dixit and funded with about $183 million. B2B software brand, with strongest recognition in Southeast Asia and India.

Raleigh, North Carolina-based CRM and marketing platform for higher education, helping colleges and universities with admissions, enrollment and student engagement. It sells subscription software with AI-driven outreach, messaging and analytics to admissions and marketing teams at US institutions. Founded in 2017 by Ardis Kadiu, who is CEO. Funding shown is about $185 million. B2B edtech software brand known to admissions teams, with no consumer profile.

Saudi online flowers and gifts retailer based in Riyadh, with delivery across the Gulf and elsewhere. It sells bouquets, plants, chocolates, cakes and gift sets directly to consumers through its app and website, using its own florists and delivery fleet, and also serves corporate gifting clients. Founded in 2017. Funding shown is about $186 million. Strong consumer brand in Saudi Arabia, Kuwait and UAE, with active marketing.

San Francisco-based automated traffic enforcement company offering AI camera systems on buses that spot illegally parked vehicles and bus lane violations. Customers are transit agencies and cities, including New York's MTA and San Francisco, and it earns revenue from hardware, software and per-violation or subscription programs. Founded in 2019 by Chris Carson. Funding shown is about $194 million. B2G brand, known in transit circles.

Nigerian infrastructure credit guarantee company, based in Lagos, providing local currency guarantees to support infrastructure project bonds. By guaranteeing bonds issued for power, transport, telecoms and similar projects it lets pension funds and other institutional investors buy them, earning guarantee fees. Founded in 2017 and owned by development finance institutions and others, including Nigeria's sovereign investment authority and GuarantCo. Funding shown is about $182 million. B2B finance brand.

London-based fashion footwear and accessories company with brands Kurt Geiger, Carvela, Miss KG and Kurt Geiger London. Founded by Kurt Geiger in 1963, it sells shoes and bags through its own stores, department store concessions such as Harrods and Selfridges, wholesale partners, and online. Privately owned. Selling in the UK, US and online. Strong consumer brand in the UK, known for its eagle-eye logo and bright designs.

US financial advisory firm in New York offering M&A, restructuring and capital advisory services. Founded in 2006 by Joseph Perella and Peter Weinberg, both veteran Wall Street dealmakers, it works for corporates, boards and institutions, earning advisory and success fees, with offices in the US, Europe and beyond. Listed on Nasdaq (PWP) since going public through a SPAC in 2021. Revenue is in the high hundreds of millions of dollars. Premium B2B brand.

Washington DC-based tech-enabled hospitality platform operating apartment-hotel units under the Placemakr and Everhome brands, offering flexible-stay rentals in cities in the US. It leases or manages whole buildings, furnishes units and rents them to guests for nights to months, using app-based check-in and shared amenities. Founded in 2016. Venture-funded with about $192 million. Consumer hospitality brand with growing regional presence.

New Zealand meat processor and marketer based in Dunedin, selling lamb, beef and venison to the NZ and international markets. Brands include Silver Fern Farms Reserve, with processing plants across both islands and customers in foodservice, retail and export markets such as the US, Europe, China and the Middle East. Co-owned by farmers and Shanghai Maling Aquarius, which bought a 50 percent stake in 2015. Revenue is in the order of NZ$3 billion. B2B and consumer meat brand.

Changsha, Hunan-based Chinese snack retail chain operating thousands of discount snack stores selling packaged snacks, drinks and bulk goods at low prices. It merged with the Zhao Yiming chain in 2023, and the combined group, Mingming Hen Mang, listed in Hong Kong in 2025 with well over ten thousand stores. Backed by investors such as Hillhouse. Consumer retail brand in China.

Operator of Florence (Amerigo Vespucci) and Pisa (Galileo Galilei) airports in Tuscany, Italy, managing passenger services, retail and cargo. Pisa is the region's main airport for low-cost and leisure traffic and Florence serves business and short-haul routes, with income from airline charges, shops and parking. Controlled by Corporacion America Italia. Listed historically on Borsa Italiana. About 8 million passengers per year. B2B airport operator with high local visibility.

Irish ocean data company that operates uncrewed surface vessels (USVs) for seabed mapping and survey, mainly for offshore wind, oil and gas and governments. Its remote-controlled XO-450 vessels carry sonar and sensors and are run from shore control centres, with operations in the UK, Europe and the US, and it sells survey data as a service rather than hardware. Funding shown is about 183 million. B2B marine technology brand.

San Jose-based cloud networking as-a-service company which provides a virtual network backbone connecting clouds, data centers and sites. Delivered on subscription from a global network of points of presence, it lets enterprises link AWS, Azure, Google Cloud and branch offices with built-in security without managing hardware. Founded in 2018 by CEO Amir Khan and Atif Khan, and venture-funded with about $176 million. B2B IT brand.

San Jose-based networking software company providing a hyperscale network operating system (ArcOS) for switches and routers (ACE platform). It runs on commodity white-box hardware from chipmakers and switch vendors, so customers such as cloud providers, telecoms and enterprises avoid proprietary lock-in and cut costs. Founded in 2016 by Keyur Patel and funded with about $168 million. B2B technology brand. Sold as software licences and subscriptions.

Dusseldorf-based enterprise conversational AI company, offering automation for customer service contact centers across voice and chat channels. Its Cognigy.AI platform builds virtual agents that handle calls and messages for large companies, sold on subscription. Founded in 2016 by Sascha Poggemann and Philipp Heltewig. Acquired by NICE in 2025 for around $955 million. Customers include Lufthansa, Toyota and Mercedes-Benz. B2B software, no consumer brand.

Electricity and gas cooperative, listed in Crunchbase at Ramsey, New Jersey, though a Connexus Energy of Ramsey, Minnesota is the state's largest electric cooperative, serving 140,000 members. The Minnesota co-op supplies homes and businesses north of the Twin Cities and is owned by its customers rather than shareholders. The location in the data may be a mix-up. Member-owned utility, regional brand.

Fort Lauderdale, Florida-based software-defined storage company, selling SANsymphony block storage virtualization and other tools to enterprises and service providers. Led by co-founder George Teixeira, it added Swarm object storage through its 2021 acquisition of Caringo and Kubernetes storage through MayaData. Revenue comes from software licences and subscriptions sold mostly via resellers. Founded in 1998. Funding shown is about $165 million. B2B software brand, known to IT infrastructure buyers.

Emeryville, California digital health company making the Eko smart stethoscope and AI algorithms that detect heart murmur and heart failure risk, used by clinicians. Its CORE and DUO devices add ECG and digital recording to the stethoscope, with software cleared by the FDA, sold to primary care practices, hospitals and health systems. Founded in 2013 by Connor Landgraf and Jason Bellet. Venture-funded with about $173 million. B2B medical brand, known to doctors.

Santa Clara, California maker of battery-free wireless sensors and cloud analytics for industrial equipment monitoring, which harvest energy from heat and vibration. Its Eversensor devices are placed on steam traps, motors and pumps, sold as a monitoring service to manufacturers and building owners. Spun out of University of Virginia and University of Michigan research, and formerly known as PsiKick. Venture-funded with about $174 million. B2B IoT brand.

Seattle-based network detection and response company, whose Reveal(x) platform analyzes network traffic for cyber threats. Founded in 2007 by Jesse Rothstein and Raja Mukerji, it sells subscriptions to security teams that want visibility into encrypted and cloud traffic. Acquired in 2021 by Bain Capital Private Equity and Crosspoint Capital for about $900 million. Customers are large enterprises and governments. B2B security brand.

Nigerian financial services group, owner of First City Monument Bank (FCMB), based in Lagos and listed on the Nigerian Exchange. Subsidiaries cover retail, commercial and investment banking, plus asset management, stockbroking and capital markets. Founded in 1982 as First City Merchant Bank, it serves individuals, small businesses and corporates across Nigeria, with Ladi Balogun as group CEO. Consumer banking brand with national recognition in Nigeria.

Adelaide-based space technology company operating nanosatellite constellations for IoT connectivity and developing ground-penetrating mineral exploration technology (ExoSphere). ExoSphere combines seismic sensors in the field with satellite links and AI to image underground deposits, sold as a service to miners. Founded in 2018 by Flavia Tata Nardini. Customers include mining firms and governments. Funding shown is about $170 million. B2B brand, known in Australian space and mining circles.

New York-based AI platform for finance and professional services firms, using large language models to search and analyze documents. Its Matrix product lets analysts query thousands of contracts, filings and reports at once, and is sold on subscription. Customers include asset managers, banks and law firms. Founded in 2020 by George Sivulka and backed by firms such as Andreessen Horowitz. Venture-funded with about $161 million. B2B brand, known in finance.

San Diego-based treasury and finance software company, offering cloud-based cash and liquidity management, payments and risk tools to large corporates. Founded in 2000 by Jean-Luc Robert, it connects to thousands of banks and sells subscriptions to corporate treasury, finance and risk teams around the world. Venture and growth investor-backed with about $167 million. B2B software brand, widely used by large corporate treasurers.

Swedish listed conglomerate (Nasdaq Stockholm: LIFCO B), headquartered in Enkoping, that acquires and runs small niche industrial businesses in dental, demolition and tools, and systems solutions. Its decentralised model keeps acquired companies independent, such as Brokk demolition robots. Chaired by main owner Carl Bennet, it has grown through dozens of acquisitions since the early 1990s. Revenue is more than SEK 25 billion. Crunchbase description appears wrong. B2B holding company with low consumer visibility.

Sunnyvale-based AI fleet safety company providing in-cab cameras and driver behavior analytics for commercial fleets. Its device warns drivers of distraction and collision risk in real time and sells subscriptions that give fleet managers coaching tools and video evidence. Customers are logistics, delivery and trucking firms. Founded in 2015 by Stefan Heck and Alex Jacobson, with SoftBank Vision Fund among its backers. Venture-funded with about $174 million. B2B telematics brand.

Global watch and accessories brand founded in 1998 in Encinitas, California by Andy Laats and Chad DiNenna, rooted in surf, skate and action sport culture. It sells watches, bags and headphones through retail partners and online, and launched a smartwatch, the Mission, in 2015. Billabong bought it in 2006 and it was later sold to Trilantic Capital Partners. Owned by private investors. Consumer brand known in action sports.

Seattle-based industrial analytics software company whose Seeq platform lets engineers analyze time-series data from plants for process manufacturers. Its Workbench and Organizer tools sit on top of historians and cloud data lakes, sold by subscription and through Microsoft Azure and AWS marketplaces. Customers include oil, pharmaceuticals and energy companies. Founded in 2013. Funding shown is about $165 million. B2B software brand.

Turkish biscuits and confectionery maker (Ulker) based in Istanbul, part of Yildiz Holding, which also owns Godiva and United Biscuits (pladis). Brands include Ulker chocolate wafers, Halley, Biskrem and Cokokrem, and it is listed on Borsa Istanbul (ULKER). Sells biscuits, chocolate, cakes and snacks in Turkey and exports to more than 100 countries. Sponsor of Turkish sports, notably Fenerbahce. Strong consumer brand.

Helsinki-based maker of high-end virtual and mixed reality headsets (XR-4, Aero), used for professional training, design and simulation by aerospace, automotive and defense customers. Founded in 2016 by Urho Konttori, its headsets blend camera passthrough with human-eye resolution displays and are sold with software subscriptions to firms such as Volvo Cars and pilot training providers. Venture-funded with about $172 million. B2B hardware brand.

Palo Alto-based software company that offers a cloud platform linking customer support with product development, founded by Dheeraj Pandey, co-founder of Nutanix, together with Manoj Agarwal. It sells subscriptions to software and technology companies that want tickets, bugs and customer feedback in a single system with AI agents, and is backed by Khosla Ventures and Mayfield. Raised about $151 million from venture investors. B2B brand, known in SaaS circles.

Israeli AI company based in Netanya whose system optimises airline pricing and revenue management in real time. Founded in 2019 by Roy Cohen and Uri Yerushalmi, its Large Market Model analyses demand and competitor fares to set prices and offers, with airlines such as Virgin Atlantic, WestJet and Azul reported as customers. Venture-funded with about $157 million. B2B aviation software, known in the airline industry.

South Korean travel super app, based in Seoul, offering tours, activities, flights and hotel booking in the Korean market. Founded in 2012 by Lee Dong-hun, it began as a marketplace connecting travellers with local guides and now sells packages and bookings for outbound Korean travellers, earning commissions. Venture-funded with about $157 million. Strong consumer brand in Korea. Operates mainly through its own app and website.

Paris-based provider of financing for zero-emission mobility, including electric vehicles and charging infrastructure, formed by EDF and Renault Group's Mobilize arm. Founded in 2020, it buys electric vehicles and chargers and leases them to companies and local authorities, backed by its two industrial shareholders. Funding shown is 140 million in unspecified currency. B2B finance brand. Revenue comes from lease payments over multi-year contracts.

Oakland-based resale technology company powering branded secondhand programs for retailers such as Patagonia, Lululemon and Arc'teryx, handling the trade-in and resale. Trove runs the website, logistics, grading and customer service behind programs such as Worn Wear, Like New and ReBird, and earns fees and a share of sales. Led by CEO Andy Ruben. Venture-funded with about $152 million. B2B brand, but its customer-facing sites are consumer-visible.

Taiwanese semiconductor foundry based in Hsinchu, listed on the Taiwan Stock Exchange and NYSE (UMC), producing mature-node chips for communication, consumer and automotive customers. Founded in 1980 as Taiwan's first private chipmaker, it spawned companies such as MediaTek, and runs fabs in Taiwan, Singapore, Japan and China. Revenue near 7 billion dollars. B2B supplier with little public brand awareness. Customers are chip designers who outsource manufacturing.

Chinese cloud computing and server maker (formerly Inspur Information), based in Beijing and listed in Shenzhen (000977). Sells servers, AI computing systems and storage to internet, telecom and government customers, including major Chinese internet platforms and cloud providers. The parent Inspur group is state-linked. A major global server brand, ranking among the top vendors worldwide by shipments. B2B, with strong enterprise visibility.

Toy and consumer products company based in Santa Monica, California, listed on Nasdaq (JAKK), making Disney Princess, Super Mario and Sonic toys, and costumes under licenses. Its Disguise unit makes costumes and its Funnoodle unit sells pool and outdoor products. Customers are retailers such as Walmart and Target, and it has been run since 1995 by co-founder Stephen Berman. Revenue about 700 million dollars. Strong licensed consumer brand.

Luxury fashion group based in Shanghai, listed on the NYSE (LANV) after a 2022 SPAC merger, owning Lanvin, Wolford, Sergio Rossi, St John Knits and Caruso. Lanvin, founded in 1889 by Jeanne Lanvin, is the oldest French couture house still operating. Majority-controlled by Fosun. Sells in global luxury markets through boutiques, department stores and e-commerce, with revenue of a few hundred million euros. Consumer luxury brand with global recognition.

Financial guaranty insurer based in New York, listed on the NYSE (AMBC), historically insuring municipal and structured finance bonds, now running off its legacy portfolio. Founded in 1971 as the American Municipal Bond Assurance Corporation, it was hit by the 2008 credit crisis, went through Chapter 11 in 2010 to 2013 and placed its main insurer in a rehabilitation structure. It is building a specialty property and casualty business, Ambac Specialty (Everspan). B2B finance brand, known to bond investors.

Industrial manufacturer based in Carnegie, Pennsylvania, listed on the NYSE (AP). Produces forged and cast rolls for steel and aluminum mills and air and liquid processing equipment, including Buffalo Pumps and Aerofin heat exchangers, with plants in the US, Europe and Asia. Customers are metal producers and industrial users. Founded in 1929 as Pittsburgh Forgings, it carries long-term asbestos liabilities. Revenue is a little over 400 million dollars. B2B industrial brand.

Nordic online fashion and lifestyle retailer based in Malmo, listed on Nasdaq Stockholm, selling clothing, shoes, beauty and home products from many brands online in Sweden, Denmark, Norway, Finland and Germany. Founded in 2007 by Hermann Haraldsson, it also runs Boozt Beauty and a large automated warehouse in Ljungby, and sells both its own and third-party brands. Revenue about SEK 11 billion. Consumer e-commerce brand with strong Nordic recognition.

Japanese confectionery and food maker based in Osaka, listed in Tokyo, best known for Pocky, Pretz, Glico caramel and Bifidus products. Founded in 1922 by Riichi Ezaki, it also sells ice cream and dairy drinks, and the illuminated runner sign in Osaka's Dotonbori is an icon. Pocky has been sold since 1966 and is exported across Asia, Europe and the Americas. Sells in Japan and exports to dozens of countries. Strong consumer snack brand worldwide.

French video game publisher in Paris, now called Pullup Entertainment, publishing titles such as A Plague Tale, Farming Simulator and Warhammer 40,000 games through labels like Focus Entertainment, Dotemu and Deck13. Founded in 1996 by Cedric Lagarrigue, it sells digital and boxed games worldwide for PC and consoles, earning revenue per title and from catalogue sales. Listed on Euronext Paris. Consumer game brand, known to gamers.

Tokyo-based Japanese conglomerate listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange (9435), best known for the Hikari mobile phone shops and telecom retail business (Softbank carrier agent), insurance and investing. Founded in 1988 by Yasumitsu Shigeta, it earns commissions from selling mobile contracts and phones through its shop network and from insurance, with investment gains an important swing factor. Revenue in the range of 700 billion yen. Consumer retail footprint in Japan.

Sunnyvale-based security robot company listed on Nasdaq (KSCP), whose autonomous patrolling robots monitor parking lots and campuses for customers on a service subscription. Founded in 2013 and led by William Santana Li, its machines include the K5 patrol robot and the K1 blue-light tower, and it went public through a 2022 Reg A+ offering. Funding shown is about $107 million. B2B brand with a visible product.

Irvine, California-based conveyor-belt sushi restaurant chain listed on Nasdaq (KRUS), with dozens of restaurants in the US. Brand from Kura Revolving Sushi Bar, a Japanese chain, and majority-owned by it. Diners pick plates from a belt and drop empty plates into a slot for a chance to win a prize in its Bikkura Pon game. The US business was founded in 2008 and went public in 2019. Consumer restaurant brand.

Fergus Falls, Minnesota-based diversified company, listed on Nasdaq (OTTR), with an electric utility, Otter Tail Power, serving the Upper Midwest in Minnesota, North Dakota and South Dakota, plus manufacturing and plastics segments. The plastics arm makes PVC pipe, and manufacturing serves industrial and recreational customers. Founded in 1907. Revenue about 1.3 billion dollars. Regional B2B and utility brand.

Toronto-based Pineapple Financial, mortgage brokerage and fintech, listed on NYSE American (PAPL). Revenue is commissions on mortgages, and it operates in Canada through a network of independent brokers using its Pineapple Connect software platform. It went public in 2023. Small-cap, with modest consumer awareness. Acts as an intermediary between borrowers and lenders such as banks and credit unions, and went public in 2023.

Pigeon Forge, Tennessee-based regional bank holding company listed on Nasdaq (SMBK), operating SmartBank in Tennessee, Alabama and Florida. Founded in 2007 in the Smoky Mountains tourist area, it grew through acquisitions and now has offices in Knoxville, Chattanooga, Nashville and Gulf Coast markets, with around $5 billion in assets. Consumer and business banking brand, regionally recognised.

Gurugram-based Indian online travel distribution company (TBO Tek), listed on NSE and BSE in 2024, a B2B marketplace connecting travel agents with hotels and airlines. Suppliers offer hotel rooms, flights, ground transport and activities, which agents book through its platform for end travellers in India and around 100 countries abroad, and it earns margins and commissions. Revenue about 15 billion rupees. B2B brand, known to travel agents.

Mortgage real estate investment trust based in the Minneapolis area, listed on the NYSE (TWO), investing in agency mortgage-backed securities and mortgage servicing rights. It is externally managed by an affiliate of PRCM Advisers and owns the RoundPoint mortgage servicing business acquired in 2020. Income is interest and servicing fees, paid out to shareholders. Financial vehicle with no consumer brand profile.

Los Angeles-based AI company developing Genius, an active inference-based AI platform that aims to build adaptive intelligent agents, and a spatial web protocol. Neuroscientist Karl Friston is chief scientist and Gabriel Rene is CEO. Listed on the Cboe Canada (VRSS) and sold as software to enterprises and developers. Funding shown is about $88 million. B2B and developer brand with niche awareness.

Silver Spring, Maryland-based blockchain infrastructure company listed on Nasdaq (BTCS), operating Ethereum validators and staking, and its own DeFi tools. Founded in 2008 and formerly Bitcoin Shop, one of the earliest US-listed blockchain firms, it now holds large amounts of ETH and compounds yield from staking. Revenue from staking rewards. Small-cap crypto brand.

Loveland, Colorado-based AI company for radiology and medical imaging, whose Enlitic platform standardizes and manages imaging data, and adds AI for hospitals. Its software sorts, anonymises and routes scans and is sold to health systems and imaging vendors, and the company is also listed on the ASX. Founded in 2014. Funding shown is about $76 million. B2B healthtech brand.

Kolkata-based Indian jewellery retailer listed on NSE and BSE in 2023, operating Senco Gold & Diamonds stores across India and online. Founded in 1994 by Suvankar Sen as a family business from a 1930s firm, it runs a large network of showrooms across eastern India and beyond, with revenue from gold and diamond jewellery sales. Strong regional consumer brand.

Minneapolis-based leisure and charter airline, listed on Nasdaq (SNCY), flying scheduled low-fare service from Minneapolis-St. Paul and charters and cargo for Amazon. Its Boeing 737 fleet flies to leisure destinations in the US, Mexico and the Caribbean, plus charter work for sports teams and the military. Agreed in early 2026 to be acquired by Allegiant. Consumer-facing airline with strong Minnesota recognition.

Greenwich, Connecticut-based holding company listed on Nasdaq (TIPT), with specialty insurance operations (Fortegra) and other investments. Fortegra sells credit protection, warranty and service contract products through lenders, retailers and dealers, and also offers specialty property and casualty cover. Revenue from insurance premiums and fees of about 2 billion dollars. Financial services brand with low consumer awareness.

Round Rock, Texas-based data center and IT services company, listed on Nasdaq (TSSI), offering data center systems integration and facilities services to government and enterprise customers. It builds and configures racks and technology for Dell and other large partners and maintains data center infrastructure. B2B brand with low consumer awareness.

Englewood, Colorado-based medical device company listed on Nasdaq (ZYXI), selling electrotherapy devices for pain management and rehabilitation, and monitoring products. Its electrotherapy products include the NexWave and TENS-type units, rented or sold to patients through doctors and billed to insurers, and it was founded by Thomas Sandgaard. Revenue from device sales and rentals. B2B medical brand.

Denver, North Carolina-based holding company listed on Nasdaq (AIRT), with overnight air cargo (Mountain Air Cargo), ground equipment and commercial jet engines. Mountain Air Cargo and CSA flies feeder routes for FedEx, and its ground support equipment business sells deicers, while another segment trades jet engines and parts. Chairman Nicholas Swenson is its controlling shareholder. Revenue from air freight and equipment. B2B brand.

West Warwick, Rhode Island-based maker of specialty printers and aerospace printing, listed on Nasdaq (ALOT). Founded in 1969 as Astro-Med, it sells QuickLabel color label printers, test and measurement data recorders and flight deck printers for aircraft. Revenue about 150 million dollars. B2B industrial technology brand. Customers include aircraft makers, airlines and industrial labs in the US and Europe.

Laguna Hills, California-based neuromorphic AI chip designer, listed on the Australian Securities Exchange (BRN), creator of the Akida processor. Its low-power chip mimics brain-style event processing for edge devices and is licensed as intellectual property, with partners such as Renesas and MegaChips. Revenue is low, from licensing and development kits. B2B semiconductor brand.

Mumbai-based stock exchange founded in 1875, Asia's oldest, listed on the NSE (BSE Ltd). Operates equity, derivatives and currency markets and the Sensex index of 30 large companies, plus SME platforms and a mutual fund distribution system. It earns trading, listing and data fees and has a GIFT City subsidiary, India INX. High visibility in Indian finance.

Melbourne-based fintech listed on the Australian Securities Exchange (DCL), enabling fractional property investment platforms, allowing investors to buy units in real estate. Each property is held in a separate trust, with investors, advisers and financial planners buying units online in sums much smaller than a whole property. Revenue is fees. Niche finance brand.

British toy and hobby company based in Margate, Kent, listed on AIM (HRN), owning Hornby model railways, Scalextric, Airfix, Corgi and Humbrol. Founded in 1901 by Frank Hornby in Liverpool, it sells through retailers and online. It also owns European model railway brands such as Jouef and Rivarossi. Revenue about 60 million pounds. Strong consumer brands in the UK.

Chicago-based holding company listed on the NYSE (KFS), with extended warranty and insurance services (IWS, Trinity), and real estate investments. Led by J.T. Fitzgerald, it acquires small private businesses and uses cash flow to compound value, modelled on a Berkshire-style approach. B2B financial brand, low awareness. It began life as a Canadian auto insurer before reinventing itself in the US.

Ottawa-based network performance monitoring company, listed on the TSX Venture Exchange (MTLO), selling Microsoft Teams monitoring software. Its Vantage DX platform and Savision tools help IT teams find faults and measure call quality in Microsoft environments, sold to enterprises and managed service providers. B2B software brand, with limited consumer visibility.

Punjab-based Indian food company, listed on NSE and BSE in 2020, maker of Cremica biscuits and bakery products plus English Oven bread. Founded in 1978 by Rajni Bector, it supplies buns and sauces to quick service restaurant chains including McDonald's, as well as selling biscuits, cookies and breads in retail. Consumer food brand in India.

Vancouver-based digital asset and blockchain company listed on the TSX Venture Exchange (NDA), with bitcoin treasury. Formerly Neptune Dash, it started by operating Dash masternodes and has since broadened into crypto yield and treasury holdings. Funding shown is about $55 million. Niche crypto brand. Revenue comes from staking rewards and investment gains.

Columbia, Maryland-based AI company listed on Nasdaq (REKR), providing roadway intelligence and license plate recognition systems for cities and agencies. Its Rekor One software and Scout cameras read plates from existing video, supporting traffic management, toll and parking operators, and public safety customers. Led by Robert Berman. B2G brand. Founded as Novume Solutions, it took the Rekor name in 2019.

Burlington-based income fund listed on the TSX (SRV.UN) that holds royalty interest in Sir Corp's restaurant brands. Sir Corp operates Jack Astor's and Scaddabush restaurants, among others, in Ontario, and the fund receives a share of their revenue and pays it to unitholders. Funding shown is about CA$68 million. Financial vehicle, low awareness.

Minneapolis-based cloud supply chain software company listed on Nasdaq (SPSC), selling retail EDI and fulfillment tools. Its network links retailers, suppliers and logistics firms so that purchase orders and invoices flow electronically, and it sells subscriptions to tens of thousands of suppliers. Founded in 2001. Revenue about 600 million dollars. B2B brand.

South Korean beauty and health tech company based in Seoul, listed on KOSPI as APR Corp, owner of Medicube skincare and A'pieu cosmetics, and beauty devices. Medicube Age-R home devices and skincare sell strongly through Amazon and global social media, with exports a key driver of its rapid sales growth. Strong growth in the US and Asia. Consumer beauty brand.

Brossard, Quebec-based company listed on the TSX Venture Exchange (ADK), using AI for retinal screening for diabetic retinopathy and related conditions. Its CARA platform analyses retinal images for eye clinics and screening programs. Revenue is small. B2B healthcare AI brand.

Webster, Texas-based company listed on NYSE American (KULR), making thermal management and battery safety products for aerospace, defense and electronics, and holding bitcoin. Its carbon fiber thermal technology came from NASA research, and it sells to space, defense and consumer electronics customers. B2B niche brand. It adopted a bitcoin treasury strategy in late 2024.

Beaumont, Texas-based AI company listed on Nasdaq (MSAI), offering multi-sensor inspection systems for industrial and utility assets. Formerly Infrared Cameras Holdings, it went public by merging with SportsMap Tech in 2023, and sells thermal imaging cameras and AI analytics to power, petrochemical and manufacturing customers. B2B brand.

Swedish online bank and consumer finance firm based in Stockholm, listed on Nasdaq Stockholm (QLIRO), providing payment services for e-commerce and consumer lending. Qliro was spun out of the CDON group and offers a checkout for online retailers, plus personal loans, credit accounts and savings accounts to consumers. Consumer-facing financial brand in Sweden.

Chinese tea beverage chain based in Shanghai (Auntie Shanghai), listed in Hong Kong in 2025, running thousands of franchised stores. Its fruit teas and grain-based milk teas are made in small outlets, with franchisees paying fees for supplies and branding. Consumer food and drink brand in China.

Austin-based fabless semiconductor company listed on Nasdaq (SLAB), supplying wireless chips for IoT. Founded in 1996, it focuses on Bluetooth, Zigbee, Z-Wave and Matter-compatible systems-on-chip used in smart home, lighting and industrial devices, and sells them to device makers and distributors. B2B brand. It bought Sigma Designs' Z-Wave business in 2018 and sold its infrastructure and automotive unit to Skyworks in 2021.

Toronto-based asset manager listed on the TSX and NYSE (SII), specializing in precious metals and real assets, with physical gold and silver trusts. Founded by Eric Sprott, it runs Sprott Physical Gold, Silver and Uranium trusts alongside ETFs and managed funds, with assets under management in the tens of billions of dollars. Financial brand, strong among investors.

Shanghai-based online game developer and operator, listed on Nasdaq (NCTY). It rose to prominence operating Blizzard's World of Warcraft in China from 2005 to 2009. Now focused on crypto and web3. Brand known in Chinese gaming. Founded in 1999 by Zhu Jun and listed on Nasdaq since 2004.

San Rafael, California-based biopharmaceutical company, listed on Nasdaq (BMRN), developing therapies for rare genetic diseases, including Vimizim, Naglazyme, Brineura, Palynziq and Voxzogo for achondroplasia. Founded in 1997, it sells to specialist hospitals and patients and also markets the gene therapy Roctavian for hemophilia A. Revenue around 3 billion dollars. B2B and specialist healthcare brand, known to rare disease communities.

Palo Alto-based biotechnology company, listed on Nasdaq (BBIO), founded by Neil Kumar in 2015, developing genetic disease therapies through a hub-and-spoke model of subsidiaries. A heart-disease drug (Attruby, acoramidis) for transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy was approved in 2024, with Bayer partnering in Europe, and infigratinib for achondroplasia is in late-stage trials. Revenue from product sales and licensing. B2B and clinical brand, known to investors and specialists.

Wireless broadband provider (WiMAX) from Bellevue, Washington, founded by Craig McCaw, that operated the Clear 4G network in the US. Backed by investors including Sprint, Comcast, Google and Intel, it sold through the Clear brand to consumers and as wholesale capacity to cable firms. Acquired in full by Sprint Nextel in 2013, and the brand has been phased out. Historical consumer internet brand.

Dallas-based wholesale data center developer and operator, building hyperscale campuses for cloud and enterprise customers in the US. Founded in 2012 by Chris Crosby, it builds and leases standardised facilities to large tenants. Owned by Brookfield and Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan. Revenue from leasing capacity. B2B brand, low public recognition.

South San Francisco-based biopharmaceutical company, listed on Nasdaq (CYTK), founded in 1997 and developing muscle-targeted heart medicines; its first drug, Myqorzo (aficamten), was approved for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. It also has omecamtiv mecarbil for heart failure and further cardiac muscle programs, with partners including Sanofi in China and Japan. B2B pharma brand, known to cardiologists and investors.

Washington DC-headquartered science and technology conglomerate, listed on the NYSE (DHR), owning life sciences brands (Beckman Coulter, Cytiva, Leica, Pall, SCIEX, Abcam, Aldevron), and diagnostics (Cepheid). Founded in 1984 by the Rales brothers, it spun off Fortive in 2016, Envista in 2019 and Veralto in 2023. Revenue about 24 billion dollars, around 63,000 employees. B2B brand known in labs and industry.

San Diego-based biotechnology company, listed on Nasdaq (HALO), whose ENHANZE drug-delivery technology enables subcutaneous administration of biologics licensed to partners such as Roche, Takeda and Bristol. Products using it include Phesgo, Darzalex Faspro and Opdivo Qvantig, and Halozyme earns royalties on partner sales. Revenue from royalties, around 1 billion dollars. B2B pharma technology brand.

Durham, North Carolina-based provider of clinical research, healthcare data and analytics to pharma companies, listed on the NYSE (IQV), formed by merger of Quintiles and IMS Health in 2016. Pharma, biotech and medical device clients outsource trials to it and buy prescription and market data from it. Revenue about 15 billion dollars with around 88,000 employees. B2B healthcare data brand.

Gaithersburg, Maryland-based vaccine developer, listed on Nasdaq (NVAX), maker of the protein-based Nuvaxovid COVID vaccine and a vaccine technology licensed to Sanofi. Its Matrix-M adjuvant is the core technology, and Sanofi paid an upfront sum under a 2024 deal to commercialise Nuvaxovid. Founded in 1987. Revenue from partnerships and sales. Brand known mainly from the COVID pandemic.

Secaucus, New Jersey-based clinical laboratory company, listed on the NYSE (DGX), one of the largest US providers of diagnostic testing and health information services for patients, doctors and employers. Spun out of Corning in 1996, it runs patient service centres and hospital lab partnerships and competes with Labcorp. Revenue about 9 billion dollars. Strong consumer-health brand in the US.

Redwood City-based clinical-stage oncology company, listed on Nasdaq (RVMD), developing RAS inhibitors for pancreatic and lung cancer. Its lead drug, daraxonrasib (RMC-6236), targets multiple RAS mutations, backed by programs against specific mutants such as G12C and G12D. Founded in 2014 and led by Mark Goldsmith. Pre-revenue. B2B biotech brand, known to investors and oncologists.

Taiwanese hypermarket chain, with RT-Mart as a retail brand operating supermarkets in Taiwan and China, part of the Taiwan-based Ruentex Group, and strongly associated with Sun Art Retail in China. Founded in Taiwan in 1996, it later merged with Auchan's China business to form Sun Art, which Alibaba took control of and then sold to DCP Capital in 2025. Customers are consumers. Funding shown is $2.88 billion. Strong consumer retail brand in Taiwan.

Gottingen-based life science equipment company listed in Frankfurt (SRT3), supplying bioprocess technologies for biopharmaceutical production, plus lab products (Sartorius Lab). Founded in 1870 and controlled by the Sartorius family, it majority-owns Sartorius Stedim Biotech in Paris. Sells to biotech and pharma makers, competing with Danaher's Cytiva. Revenue around 3 billion euros. B2B brand.

Denver-based construction materials company producing aggregates, cement and ready-mix concrete across the US and British Columbia. Founded in 2009 and listed on the NYSE (SUM), it bought Argos USA's cement business in 2024. Agreed in 2025 to be acquired by Quikrete Holdings. Customers are contractors and public infrastructure agencies. B2B brand.

Miami-based clinical-stage biotech company, listed on Nasdaq (SMMT), developing ivonescimab, a PD-1/VEGF bispecific antibody for cancer, licensed from Akeso. Led by Robert Duggan and Maky Zanganeh, it paid Akeso an upfront sum in 2022 for rights outside China and some other regions and is running lung cancer trials. Pre-revenue. B2B pharma brand known to investors.

Dallas-based healthcare services company, listed on the NYSE (THC), operating acute care hospitals and ambulatory surgery centers (USPI) across the US, with revenue of about 20 billion dollars. The USPI unit is among the largest surgery center operators, and Conifer provides revenue cycle services. Founded in 1967 as National Medical Enterprises. Customers are patients and insurers. Regional hospital brand.

San Carlos, California-based vaccine company, listed on Nasdaq (PCVX), developing next-generation pneumococcal conjugate vaccines (VAX-31). Founded in 2013, it uses a cell-free protein synthesis platform licensed from Sutro Biopharma and competes with Pfizer's Prevnar and Merck's Capvaxive. Pre-revenue. B2B biotech brand. Its earlier VAX-24 candidate showed strong adult data, and the company has no marketed product yet.

Boston-based biotech, listed on Nasdaq (VRTX), best known for cystic fibrosis medicines (Trikafta) and expanding into pain (Journavx), sickle cell (Casgevy, with CRISPR Therapeutics) and kidney disease. Founded in 1989, it sells to specialist hospitals and clinics worldwide. Revenue about 11 billion dollars. B2B pharma brand with strong patient community recognition.

Colombian airline group, headquartered in Bogota and the national flag carrier (Avianca), with a hub at El Dorado Airport, flying across the Americas and to Europe. Founded in 1919, it is among the world's oldest airlines still operating, a Star Alliance member with the LifeMiles loyalty program. Its ownership included Abra Group (with Gol) after the 2020 bankruptcy. Consumer airline with strong Latin American recognition.

Aventura, Florida-based property developer, including Fontainebleau resorts in Miami Beach and Las Vegas, owned by the Soffer family. The Miami Beach hotel dates from 1954, and the Las Vegas resort opened in late 2023. Customers are hotel guests and condo buyers. Strong consumer hospitality brand. The resort pairs a landmark mid-century hotel with a large Las Vegas casino resort off the Strip.

New Delhi-based Indian infrastructure group developing and operating airports (Delhi, Hyderabad, Goa), power, roads and urban infrastructure. Founded in 1978 by G. M. Rao, who runs it with his family, and privately held by the Grandhi Mallikarjuna Rao family. It also co-owns the IPL cricket team Delhi Capitals. Strong brand in Indian infrastructure.

Nigeria-founded, London-headquartered mobile tower company listed on the NYSE (IHS), owning about 40,000 towers across Nigeria, Brazil and Africa. Founded in 2001, it leases space on towers to operators and earns long-term contracted rental revenue, going public in 2021. Customers are mobile operators such as MTN. B2B infrastructure brand.

Turkish conglomerate in construction, cement, energy, tourism and airport operations (Pristina, Istanbul new airport as part of a consortium), based in Ankara. Founded in 1976 and led by chairman Nihat Ozdemir, it also runs hotels and builds roads, dams and airports. Privately owned. Builds major infrastructure around the world. Corporate brand in Turkey.

Elkhart, Indiana-based supplier of components for the RV, marine, and manufactured housing industries, listed on Nasdaq (PATK). Founded in 1959, it makes and distributes cabinets, doors, flooring, countertops and electronics, and serves powersports firms. Customers are manufacturers and RV makers such as Thor and Forest River. Revenue about 3.7 billion dollars. B2B brand.

London-based education finance provider for international students, giving loans to study at top universities. Founded in 2007, it lends without cosigners or collateral, basing decisions on the student's future earning potential, and funds the loans from institutional investors. Venture-funded. Consumer-facing for students. Moderate recognition in education. Its customers are mainly graduate students heading to the US, UK and other major study destinations.

San Francisco-based construction and engineering group described by Crunchbase as one of the largest building and infrastructure engineering and construction groups. Funding shown is $1.9 billion. B2B construction brand. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Swedish engineering group in Stockholm, listed on Nasdaq Stockholm (SAND), producing mining equipment, rock tools and metal-cutting tools (Sandvik Coromant). Founded in 1862, it has divisions for mining and rock solutions, rock processing and manufacturing and machining solutions, and spun off its materials business as Alleima in 2022. About 40,000 employees. Revenue about SEK 120 billion. Strong B2B brand.

Osaka theme park operator, Universal Studios Japan, with attractions including Super Nintendo World, Harry Potter and Minions areas. Opened in 2001 and owned by Comcast (NBCUniversal) since 2017, after buying out the remaining shares. Revenue is from tickets, merchandise and food, and it has seasonal events and corporate sponsors. Receives over 15 million visitors a year. Strong consumer brand in Japan, active in marketing partnerships.

Dallas-based engineering and infrastructure consulting firm, listed on the NYSE (ACM), providing design, program management and construction services for governments and corporations in transportation, water and energy. Formed in 1990, it works worldwide, with a large share of revenue from US public agencies. Revenue about 16 billion dollars with around 50,000 employees. B2B brand.

Madison, New Jersey-based residential real estate services company (formerly Realogy), listed on the NYSE (HOUS), owning brands Coldwell Banker, Century 21, Sotheby's International Realty, ERA, Better Homes and Gardens Real Estate and Corcoran, and the Cartus relocation business. It also owns title and mortgage joint ventures and earns franchise fees and commissions. Revenue about 5.7 billion dollars. Agreed to be acquired by Compass in 2025. Strong consumer brands.

Newton, Massachusetts-based provider of employer-sponsored child care, early education and back-up care, listed on the NYSE (BFAM), operating more than 1,000 centers across the US, UK and Netherlands. Founded in 1986 by Linda Mason and Roger Brown, it contracts with employers who pay for on-site and nearby centers as a staff benefit. Revenue about 2.5 billion dollars. Consumer brand among working parents.

Phoenix-based specialty contractor for utilities, listed on the NYSE (CTRI), providing natural gas and electric infrastructure construction and maintenance in North America. Formerly part of Southwest Gas, which took it public in 2024, it is paid under long-term contracts by utilities. Revenue above 2 billion dollars. B2B brand.

Irvine, California-based commercial real estate firm, offering investment and development services, per its Crunchbase listing. Funding shown is $1.42 billion. B2B brand with low public awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Shanghai-based AI chip company designing training and inference chips for data centers, backed by Tencent. Founded in 2018, its Cloud Suixi accelerator cards compete with Nvidia products in Chinese cloud and internet customers' servers. Filed for a Shanghai STAR Market IPO in 2025. B2B technology brand.

Singapore-headquartered executive education platform partnering with top universities (Harvard, MIT, Wharton), offering online programs for professionals. Founded in 2010 in India by Ashwin Damera and Chaitanya Kalipatnapu, it merged with Emeritus and sells courses to individuals and companies globally. Venture-funded and valued in the billions of dollars at its peak. B2B and consumer education brand.

Beijing-based Chinese baijiu liquor company, Guanyun Liquor, brewing and selling spirits. Funding shown is CN¥10 billion. Consumer alcohol brand in China. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Hong Kong-based property developer listed on the HKEX (101), developing commercial properties such as Plaza 66 in Shanghai and malls across mainland China. Its Grand Gateway 66 and Center 66 projects in other cities carry the 66 brand, and the company also owns Hong Kong office and retail buildings. Controlled by the Chen family. Strong local brand.

Spanish office property group, Inmobiliaria Colonial, based in Barcelona and listed in Madrid (COL), owning prime offices in Paris, Madrid and Barcelona (merged with SFL). The French unit Societe Fonciere Lyonnaise holds Paris landmark buildings, and tenants are large companies. Criteria Caixa and Qatar Investment Authority have been major shareholders. B2B real estate brand.

Medical device company developing targeted lung denervation, a bronchoscopic procedure that treats chronic obstructive pulmonary disease by disrupting nerve signals to the airways. Formerly called Holaira, it ran the AIRFLOW-3 pivotal trial. Based in Maple Grove, Minnesota, and venture-backed. B2B medtech with limited public awareness.

Indian school education technology company providing integrated curriculum, teaching tools, and digital classroom products to private schools, selling subscriptions through a large school network. Founded in 2012 by Sumeet Mehta and Smita Deorah. Based in Mumbai and venture-backed. B2B to schools with strong brand among parents in small Indian cities.

Infant health company that makes Evivo, a probiotic containing a specific Bifidobacterium strain (B. infantis EVC001) for newborn gut health, sold via consumer subscription, hospitals and healthcare channels. The strain was developed from University of California, Davis research on breast milk sugars. Founded as Evolve Biosystems and based in Sacramento, venture-backed. Consumer-facing brand with modest awareness among new parents.

US flatbed and specialised trucking group formed by acquiring many carriers, including Lone Star Transportation and Bulldog Hiway Express, hauling steel, building materials and oversized loads, listed on Nasdaq as DSKE. Founded in 2008 by Don Daseke. It was acquired by TFI International in 2024. Based in Addison, Texas. B2B freight carrier with no consumer brand.

Chinese SaaS company that provides e-commerce tools for merchants to run online stores, social commerce and retail operations through the Youzan platform. Tencent-backed and tied closely to WeChat mini-programs, it earns revenue from subscriptions and payment-related fees. Based in Hangzhou and listed in Hong Kong. B2B, with brand awareness among Chinese merchants.

US biotechnology company developing drugs against MRGPRX2 and other receptors for itch and inflammatory conditions such as chronic urticaria, including EP262. Based in San Diego and privately held, it was acquired by Incyte in 2024 for about 750 million dollars upfront. Customers would be dermatology patients. Research-stage company with no consumer profile.

US gene therapy company in Alachua, Florida, listed on Nasdaq (AGTC), developing AAV treatments for inherited eye diseases such as X-linked retinitis pigmentosa and achromatopsia. Spun out of University of Florida research and partnered with Biogen on XLRP. Acquired by Syncona in 2022. Customers would have been ophthalmologists and patients. Research-stage firm with no consumer profile.

US biotechnology company in Cambridge, Massachusetts, developing amino acid compositions to treat liver and metabolic diseases such as NASH, with lead candidate AXA1125. Listed on Nasdaq (AXLA) and ceased operations in 2023 after trial setbacks. Customers would have been hepatologists and patients. Research-stage firm with no consumer profile.

Chinese oncology and metabolic disease biotech developing targeted drugs such as afuresertib, an AKT inhibitor licensed from GSK, and other candidates in trials across Asia. It also has LAE102, an antibody aimed at obesity. Based in Shanghai. Customers would be oncologists and patients. Research-stage firm with no consumer profile.

Danish biotechnology company developing small-molecule drugs for rare neuromuscular diseases such as myasthenia gravis, including NMD670. Founded in 2018 by researchers from Aarhus University. Based near Aarhus. Funded by venture and strategic investors. Customers would be neurologists and patients. Research-stage firm with no consumer profile.

US pharmaceutical company developing anti-infectives for drug-resistant bacterial infections, notably cefepime-taniborbactam for complicated urinary tract infections, which received an FDA complete response letter in 2024. Menarini holds rights outside the US. Based in Malvern, Pennsylvania. Funded by venture investors and government grants. Customers would be hospitals. Research-stage firm with no consumer profile.

US cell therapy company in Philadelphia, listed on Nasdaq (CARM), developing engineered macrophage (CAR-M) therapies for solid tumours, with partners such as Moderna. A University of Pennsylvania spin-out, it went public in 2023 by merging with Sesen Bio. Customers would be oncologists and patients. Research-stage firm with no consumer profile.

Canadian-US biotechnology company developing VAL-083, a chemotherapy for glioblastoma, a brain cancer. Formerly DelMar Pharmaceuticals, it was listed on Nasdaq (KTRA), with offices in Vancouver and San Diego. Merged with TuHURA Biosciences in 2024. Customers would have been oncologists and patients. Small research-stage firm with no consumer profile.

South Korean biotechnology company listed on KOSDAQ, developing antibody-based cancer immunotherapy, including IMC-001, a PD-L1 antibody, and IMC-002, a CD47 antibody. Founded as a joint venture between Yuhan and Sorrento. Based in Seoul. Customers would be oncologists and patients. Small research-stage firm with no consumer profile.

Israeli additive manufacturing company with NanoParticle Jetting technology, which prints metal and ceramic parts with fine detail for aerospace, medical, dental and industrial users. Founded in 2005 by Hanan Gothait, who previously co-founded Objet. Based in Rehovot. Customers are manufacturers buying printers and materials. B2B industrial brand known among advanced manufacturing engineers.

Swedish diagnostics company with blood tests to detect pancreatic cancer early, notably IMMray PanCan-d and PancreaSure for people at high risk. Founded in 2007 in Lund, with a US laboratory in Massachusetts. Listed on Nasdaq Stockholm and based in Lund. Customers are doctors and laboratories. Small diagnostics firm with niche awareness.

Finnish medical technology company that makes navigated brain stimulation systems (NBS) using transcranial magnetic stimulation for mapping brain function before surgery and for treating depression. Its depression therapy (NBT) received FDA clearance in 2017. Listed on Nasdaq Helsinki and based in Helsinki. Customers are hospitals and neurosurgeons. Small medtech company with niche awareness.

US biotechnology company in Massachusetts developing AC5, a peptide-based hemostatic gel to stop surgical bleeding and speed wound healing, sold under the AC5 Advanced Wound System. The self-assembling peptide technology originated at MIT. Listed on the over-the-counter markets (ARTH). Customers are surgeons and hospitals. Small medtech company with no consumer profile.

Belgian specialty pharmaceutical company, listed on Euronext Brussels, developing improved versions of existing drugs for the US and European hospitals, using a 505(b)(2) pathway. Products include Sotalol IV and Maxigesic IV, the latter partnered with AFT Pharmaceuticals. Founded in 2012 and based in Liege. Customers are hospitals and pharma partners. Small pharma business with modest recognition among investors.

Canadian-US pharmaceutical company developing NX-1207 (fexapotide triflutate) for benign prostatic hyperplasia and other urology and diagnostic products, including the AD7C-NTP test for Alzheimer's. Founded by Paul Averback and listed on Nasdaq (NYMX) until it was delisted, and run from Hasbrouck Heights, New Jersey, with Montreal roots. Customers would be urologists and patients. Small drug developer with no consumer profile.

US biopharmaceutical company developing suramin, a drug for autism spectrum disorder and related neurodevelopmental conditions. Listed on Nasdaq (PXMD) after an IPO in 2022 and based in Tarrytown, New York. Customers would be patients and physicians. Small research-stage firm with no consumer profile.

Seattle biotech founded in 1981, originally linked to Novo Nordisk, that developed Recothrom thrombin and co-developed romiplostim (Nplate) with Amgen, as well as the interleukin-21 programme. Revenue came from product sales and partner royalties. Listed on Nasdaq as ZGEN. Bristol-Myers Squibb acquired it in 2010 for about $885 million. No longer independent.

US maker of compact ultrasound imaging systems (ZONE Sonography) sold to hospitals and clinics, headquartered in New Jersey after earlier California roots. Venture backed. Acquired by China's Mindray in 2013 for about 105 million dollars. B2B medical imaging, no consumer brand.

California medical device company (Mountain View) with the AeroForm tissue expander, a patient-controlled device for breast reconstruction after mastectomy, sold to plastic surgeons and hospitals. Listed on the Australian Securities Exchange. It entered Chapter 11 in 2019 and its assets were sold to Sientra. B2B device with low public visibility.

Suzhou-based Chinese medical device company developing transcatheter heart valve systems, including aortic valve replacement and mitral devices, such as the TaurusOne and TaurusElite. It sells to hospitals in China. Listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange since 2021. Medical device brand with low public awareness.

Perth-based mineral sands developer with the Thunderbird project in Western Australia's Canning Basin, holding zircon, ilmenite and rare earth-bearing sands. Chinese steelmaker Yansteel became a partner in the project. Sells to pigment and ceramics producers and was seeking offtake and funding. Listed on the Australian Securities Exchange. No consumer brand.

Vancouver gold producer with mines in Nicaragua and Nevada, and Newfoundland projects, notably the Valentine gold project acquired through Marathon Gold in 2024. Listed on the TSX. Merged into Equinox Gold in 2025. Commodity miner, no consumer brand.

Paris medical imaging company founded in 2000 behind the EOS system, a low-dose 2D/3D X-ray scanner of the spine and legs in standing position, sold to hospitals and orthopaedic clinics. Listed on Euronext Paris. Alphatec Spine acquired it in 2020. B2B device brand with low public profile.

Frankfurt-based German commercial real estate company with office properties in German cities, listed in Frankfurt. Revenue comes from rents. No consumer brand profile. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Mumbai Indian pharma maker of branded generics and drug ingredients, strongest in malaria drugs, pain relief and cardiac products, with brands such as Lariago, Zerodol and HCQS sold in India and exports. Founded in 1949, it also holds a stake in Unichem. Listed on NSE and BSE. Known to Indian doctors, with limited consumer awareness elsewhere.

Tokyo company that owns and operates shared telecom infrastructure: in-building antenna systems and rooftop or ground towers rented to mobile network operators such as NTT Docomo, KDDI, SoftBank and Rakuten. Founded in 2012. Listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange growth market. B2B infrastructure, no consumer brand.

South Korean maker of botulinum toxin products, mainly Meditoxin, Innotox and Coretox, plus hyaluronic acid fillers, sold to clinics and exported to many countries. Founded in 2000 by Chung Hyun-ho. Listed on KOSDAQ. Involved in an import dispute with Daewoong. B2B aesthetics supplier with brand awareness in cosmetic medicine.

Indian hospital group in Bangalore, founded by cardiac surgeon Devi Shetty in 2000, running multi-specialty hospitals, with a focus on low-cost cardiac surgery, across India with about 6,000 beds and a Cayman Islands presence (Health City). Listed on NSE and BSE since 2015. Well known in India healthcare.

Kolkata diagnostics chain that runs pathology labs and imaging centres in eastern India with patient collection points. Customers are patients and doctors. Listed on the Indian exchanges in 2025. Regional healthcare brand.
Vancouver-based gold developer and producer with the Segilola gold mine in Nigeria, plus the Douta project in Senegal, listed on AIM in London and the TSX Venture. Commodity miner, no consumer brand.

Hangzhou Chinese medical device company developing transcatheter heart valves (VenusA, Venus-P), sold to hospitals in China and abroad. Founded in 2009 and listed in Hong Kong, it also took a stake in Israeli firm Cardiovalve. Medical device brand with little public awareness.

Hyderabad, India diagnostics chain operating pathology labs, radiology centres and sample collection points across many Indian cities. Founded in 1981 by Dr. S. Surendranath Reddy. Customers are patients and doctors. Listed on NSE and BSE since 2021. Regional healthcare brand with solid reach in south India.

New York company with the Dragon Mine in Utah, producing halloysite clay (Dragonite) and iron oxide for industrial customers. Listed in the US over the counter. Small commodity firm, no consumer brand.

Swiss maker of vacuum instruments and gas analysis equipment, serving semiconductor, vacuum coating, HVAC leak detection, and emergency response customers. Based in Bad Ragaz. Listed on the SIX Swiss Exchange, with operations in the US, Germany and Asia. B2B technology firm with industrial recognition.

US spinal surgery device maker (complex spine and minimally invasive spine), based in Leesburg, Virginia. Founded in 2004 by Eric Major and listed on Nasdaq as KTWO since 2014. Stryker acquired it in 2018 for about $1.4 billion. B2B medical device brand.

Oslo biometrics company making fingerprint-sensing payment cards (Zwipe Pay) and access cards, sold to card manufacturers, banks and payment companies in Europe, Asia, and the US. Listed on Euronext Growth Oslo. Lost major customers after 2022 and cut costs. B2B component with little consumer awareness.

Romanian state-controlled pharma maker in Valea Lupului near Iasi, producing antibiotics and generic medicines, including penicillin and semi-synthetic antibiotics, sold in Romania and exported. Founded in 1955. Listed on the Bucharest Stock Exchange. Local brand, mostly B2B and pharmacy distribution.

Johannesburg-based vanadium company that owns the Vametco mine and processing plant in South Africa, plus the Brazilian Largo vanadium stake, selling vanadium for steel alloying and energy storage. Its Bushveld Energy unit works on vanadium flow batteries. Listed on London's AIM. B2B commodity producer, no consumer brand.

Korean-American rehabilitation technology company making smart gloves (Rapael) and digital therapy devices for stroke patients to practise hand movement at home or clinic, with software tracking. Sells to hospitals and patients in Korea, US and Europe. Listed in Korea. Niche medical brand.

Indian educational publisher in New Delhi, founded in 1939, that publishes school textbooks, reference books, test prep and digital learning content, sold through schools and bookshops. It acquired publishers including Vikas Publishing. Listed on NSE and BSE since 2017. Familiar to Indian students and parents.

Florida medical device company whose SRT-100 systems deliver superficial radiation therapy for non-melanoma skin cancer, sold to dermatologists and clinics. Based in Boca Raton, listed on Nasdaq as SRTS since 2016. B2B device brand.

New Jersey critical-care pharma company behind INOmax (inhaled nitric oxide) for newborns with respiratory failure, plus other hospital products. Spun off its Bellerophon unit in 2014. Customers are hospitals. Acquired by Mallinckrodt in 2014 for about $2.3 billion. B2B pharma.

Danish biotech in Ballerup developing antibody mixtures (Sym004, Sym015) for cancer. Founded in 2000. Servier acquired it in 2017. Funded by venture investors and partnerships. B2B biotech, no consumer profile.

Seattle cell therapy company developing CAR-T treatments for cancer. Founded 2013 with ties to Fred Hutchinson, Memorial Sloan Kettering and Seattle Children's, listed on Nasdaq as JUNO in 2014, and acquired by Celgene in 2018 for about $9 billion; Bristol-Myers Squibb later bought Celgene and sells its Breyanzi CAR-T. B2B biotech.

Pennsylvania regenerative medicine company developing organs grown from patient cells (kidney, bladder), including the Neo-Urinary Conduit. Listed on Nasdaq, filed for bankruptcy in 2014. B2B biotech.
Kentucky specialty pharmaceutical company selling pain medicines, including Zipsor and the Darvocet analgesic family until its 2010 withdrawal. Private equity backed. B2B pharma, no consumer profile.

Irish-domiciled biopharma in Dublin, with US operations, selling Vivitrol, Aristada and Lybalvi for addiction and schizophrenia, and partner royalties, notably on Invega Sustenna. Founded in 1987 and listed on Nasdaq as ALKS. B2B pharma with doctor brand awareness.

Finnish drug developer in Turku focused on central nervous system disease, especially Parkinson's (tozadenant). Founded in 1988 and listed in Helsinki and Nasdaq. Acorda Therapeutics acquired it in 2016. B2B biotech.

Missouri specialty pharma (St Louis) selling Makena, a preterm birth prevention injection, and other women's health products. Formerly KV Pharmaceutical, renamed Lumara Health in 2013. AMAG Pharmaceuticals acquired it in 2014 for about $675 million. B2B pharma.

US respiratory biotech developing inhaled combination therapies for COPD and asthma using its co-suspension delivery technology, leading to Bevespi and Breztri. AstraZeneca acquired it in 2013 for about $1.15 billion. B2B pharma, no consumer brand.

New Jersey pharmaceutical company that sold Lovaza (omega-3, formerly Omacor) for high triglycerides and cardiovascular medicines. GlaxoSmithKline bought it in 2007 for about $1.65 billion. B2B pharma.

Vancouver biopharma developing inflammatory disease drugs (AQX-1125, rosiptor) for bladder pain, which failed a Phase 3 trial in 2018. Merged with Neoleukin Therapeutics in 2019. Listed on Nasdaq. B2B biotech.

Massachusetts oncology biotech developing targeted cancer drugs (tivantinib, ARQ 092, ARQ 087 derazantinib, ARQ 531). Listed on Nasdaq as ARQL. Merck acquired it in 2019 for about $2.7 billion; ARQ 531 became nemtabrutinib. B2B pharma, no consumer brand.

Cambridge, Massachusetts cell therapy company using pluripotent stem cells to develop treatments for Parkinson's and other disease, including bemdaneprocel. Co-founded by Versant and Arch; Bayer acquired it in 2019 for about $600 million upfront. B2B biotech.

Montreal rare disease company developing palovarotene for fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP), later approved as Sohonos. Listed on Nasdaq as CMTA; acquired by Ipsen in 2019 for about $1.3 billion. B2B pharma.

South San Francisco genetic testing company, founded in 2007, known for carrier screening of prospective parents for inherited disease (Family Prep Screen), sold via doctors and directly to patients. Myriad Genetics acquired it in 2018 for about $375 million. Moderate consumer familiarity through physicians.
Shanghai diabetes drug developer behind dorzagliatin, a glucokinase activator, approved in China in 2022. Bayer is its commercial partner there. Listed on Hong Kong Stock Exchange (2552). B2B pharma.
Seattle immuno-oncology biotech developing vaccine adjuvants (GLA) and cancer vaccines (CMB305, G100). Listed on Nasdaq as IMDZ. Merck acquired it in 2019 for about $300 million. B2B biotech.
Cambridge, UK antibody developer using mice with human antibody genes. Its lead antibody KY1005 became Sanofi's amlitelimab. Sanofi acquired it in 2021 for about $1.1 billion upfront. B2B biotech.

Geneva-area biotech (Light Chain Bioscience, formerly Novimmune) developing antibody therapies for immune-mediated disease, with emapalumab (Gamifant) licensed to Sobi. Private, funded by investors. B2B biotech.

Swiss women's health biotech (Geneva) developing linzagolix and nolasiban for endometriosis and fibroids; linzagolix was approved in Europe as Yselty. Listed on Nasdaq and Swiss exchange; wound down after funding trouble in 2022 to 2023. B2B biotech.

Vaccine company that sold Vaxchora (cholera) and Vivotif (typhoid) travel vaccines, with manufacturing in Bern, Switzerland. Emergent BioSolutions acquired it in 2018 for about $270 million. B2B pharma.

Dallas biotech, not the fitness company, developing HIF-2 alpha inhibitors for kidney cancer, the origin of belzutifan (Welireg). Merck acquired it in 2019 for about $1.05 billion upfront. B2B biotech.

Las Vegas cannabis company running Planet 13, a large dispensary and entertainment superstore on Las Vegas near the Strip, plus wholesale and Orange County and Illinois sites. Founded by Robert Groesbeck and Larry Scheffler. Listed on the Canadian Securities Exchange. Consumer-facing cannabis brand with tourist visibility.
Cambridge, Massachusetts biotech developing zilucoplan for myasthenia gravis, later approved as Zilbrysq. UCB acquired it in 2020 for about $2.2 billion. B2B pharma.

South San Francisco oncology drug developer working on vosaroxin, which failed its Phase 3 VALOR trial in leukemia. Founded in 1998. Merged with Viracta Therapeutics in 2021. Listed on Nasdaq as SNSS. B2B biotech.

Philadelphia cell therapy company founded by University of Pennsylvania researchers including Carl June, developing engineered T-cell therapies for cancer and autoimmune disease; Gilead's Kite unit acquired it in 2023. B2B biotech.
Israeli medical device company (V-Wave) developing the Ventura interatrial shunt for heart failure; Johnson & Johnson MedTech acquired it in 2024. B2B medical device.

Philippines property developer in Mandaluyong that builds affordable condo and housing projects (Urban Deca Homes, Deca Homes), led by chairman Mariano Martinez. Listed on the Philippine Stock Exchange. Local consumer-facing real estate brand known among middle-income buyers.

San Diego diagnostics company behind NephroCheck, a test for acute kidney injury risk that measures the biomarkers TIMP-2 and IGFBP7 on its Astute140 meter. bioMerieux acquired it in 2018. B2B diagnostics.

Swedish medtech from Lund making Cerament (including Cerament G and V), an injectable bone graft substitute for fractures and bone infections, sold in Europe and the US. Founded in 1999 and listed on Nasdaq Stockholm. B2B.

Irvine, California endovascular device maker (AFX, Ovation, Nellix) treating abdominal aortic aneurysm, sold to hospitals. Listed on Nasdaq as ELGX; filed Chapter 11 in 2020 and its assets sold to Deerfield. B2B.
California maker of swallowable gastric balloons for weight loss, with the Obalon Balloon System approved by the FDA in 2016; merged with ReShape Lifesciences in 2021. Listed on Nasdaq. B2B medtech.

UK diagnostics company, founded from Oxford University research, with the T-SPOT.TB test for tuberculosis infection, sold to labs and hospitals. Listed on Nasdaq as OXFD; PerkinElmer acquired it in 2021 for about $591 million. B2B.
Massachusetts oncology biotech with ganetespib, which failed a Phase 3 lung cancer trial in 2015; merged with Madrigal Pharmaceuticals in 2016. B2B biotech.
Minnesota medtech selling balloon sinus dilation (XprESS) for chronic sinusitis. Stryker acquired it in 2018 for about $662 million. B2B.
South San Francisco antibiotic developer that gained approval for Zemdri (plazomicin) in 2018, then filed for bankruptcy in 2019, with Zemdri sold to Cipla. B2B pharma.
Genomic diagnostics company with MammaPrint and BluePrint for breast cancer recurrence risk and subtyping, based in Amsterdam and Irvine. Private, with listed ties. B2B diagnostics.
California pharma with Adasuve, an inhaled drug for agitation in schizophrenia using its Staccato technology; Ferrer acquired it in 2016. B2B pharma.
Kansas animal health biotech developing pet drugs such as Entyce and Galliprant for dogs; Elanco acquired it in 2019 for about $255 million. B2B vet pharma.
Biopharma that markets Giapreza for septic shock, based in Waltham, Massachusetts and founded in San Diego in 1989. Listed on Nasdaq as LJPC until Innoviva acquired it in 2022. B2B pharma.
California agricultural biotech founded by Pam Marrone, making biopesticides (Regalia, Venerate, Grandevo, Stargus). Bioceres Crop Solutions acquired it in 2022. B2B agri-input.
Cambridge, Massachusetts biotech developing cystic fibrosis therapies; merged with Yumanity in 2020, and the combined company later merged with Kineta. B2B biotech.
California ophthalmic device maker with PRESBYLENS (earlier the Raindrop Near Vision Inlay), a corneal inlay for presbyopia. Private. B2B.
New York oncology biotech with Elzonris for blastic plasmacytoid dendritic cell neoplasm and later Orserdu; Menarini acquired it in 2020 for about $677 million. B2B pharma.

Irish biopharma (Strongbridge, Trevose PA operations) that sold Keveyis for periodic paralysis and Macrilen for diagnosing adult growth hormone deficiency, both for rare endocrine disease. Xeris Pharmaceuticals acquired it in 2021. B2B pharma.
San Diego biotech with Toca 511 gene therapy for brain cancer, whose Phase 3 trial failed in 2019; merged with Forte Biosciences in 2020. B2B biotech.
